title: When does active intervention still pay after probe cost and dense hidden causes?
competing_explanations: The main advantage is causal: choosing interventions reveals hidden structure that passive observation cannot recover, so the benefit should persist after charging a realistic probe budget.
The observed advantage depends strongly on sparse causes and cheap interventions; as hidden causes become dense or probes become costly, passive or random strategies may catch up.
known: GeometricNeuronV24 shows that addressed stimulation can remove an algebraic ambiguity left by a fixed soma observation, although practical identity remains noise-limited.
ReadWrite gives a deterministic existence proof that a state-dependent write can reveal measurement-nullspace information that passive reading and a constant write cannot.
LentoOrava shows large scalar-only localization gains over equal-budget random probing in sparse synthetic fault worlds.
missing_discriminator: A matched-budget sweep that jointly varies intervention cost and hidden-cause density while keeping the observation channel and repair/action budget fixed.

candidate_experiment.design: Build one synthetic hidden-state benchmark with a tunable number of simultaneous causes. Compare adaptive intervention, random intervention, and passive observation at equal total cost, where each probe and each repair consumes explicit budget. Sweep cause density from sparse to dense and report recovery/identification quality against cost.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: one reusable synthetic benchmark, roughly 20-50 seeds per density/cost cell, CPU-friendly

outcomes.if: Adaptive intervention keeps a stable advantage over random/passive strategies across increasing cause density after equalizing total cost
outcomes.then: The cross-repo active-intervention motif gains evidence that is less dependent on sparse causes or free probing.

outcomes.if: The advantage collapses as density or probe cost rises while random/passive strategies converge to the same quality-cost frontier
outcomes.then: The motif should be narrowed to sparse or inexpensive-intervention regimes rather than treated as a general advantage.

notes: This question does not assume that active intervention is universally superior; it asks where the existing advantage stops.

title: Is late relevance an architectural advantage once training fit is equalized?
competing_explanations: Keeping richer state resident and applying relevance nearer publication creates a genuine switch/readiness advantage even when competing models fit the training distribution equally well.

The large FusionMachine readiness gap is mostly explained by unequal training fit, while the clean NewMachine result reflects a narrower factorization benefit rather than a broad architectural advantage.
known: FusionMachine shows a large readiness/switch gap, but its generic recurrent baseline also fits the training queries substantially worse.
NewMachine isolates a smaller factorization benefit under overlapping reliability and publication constraints while keeping state repair decisions matched.
missing_discriminator: A readiness comparison in which late-relevance and generic baselines are matched to the same training-query error before dormant/switch evaluation.

candidate_experiment.design: Train multiple late-relevance and generic recurrent baselines until each model enters the same narrow training-error band, using extra optimization or capacity only to equalize fit. Freeze parameters, then measure first-query-after-switch and post-dormancy error on held-out worlds.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: reuse FusionMachine task generator and add fit-matching/rejection logic across 16-32 seeds

outcomes.if: Late-relevance models retain a switch/dormancy advantage after training-query error is tightly matched
outcomes.then: The architectural interpretation gains direct support beyond the current training-quality confound.

outcomes.if: The readiness gap largely disappears once training fit is matched
outcomes.then: The current FusionMachine effect should be attributed mainly to optimization/fit differences, leaving NewMachine's narrower factorization result as the cleaner survivor.

notes: Partially resolved means one narrower construction is clean while the broader readiness claim remains confounded.

title: What survives from bounded observation: active addressing or a particular grid code?
competing_explanations: Most of the robust gain comes from choosing informative addresses or interventions; the exact multiscale/coprime code is secondary.
Specific structured measurement families still provide an independent advantage, but the existing matched-budget attacker was not the right regime to expose it.
known: GeometricNeuronV24 replicates active address selection while fixed-scale active sensing can match the multiscale variant, weakening a unique multiscale interpretation.
ReadWrite's coprime grid stack fails to beat the best single grid by its registered matched-budget threshold.
ReadWrite's state-dependent active write still reveals hidden-state distinctions that passive reading cannot.
missing_discriminator: A factorial experiment separating adaptivity from measurement-family structure at the same number of probes, same spatial support, and same noise level.

candidate_experiment.design: Cross adaptive versus fixed address selection with structured versus unstructured probe families. Use identical probe counts and matched receptive-field area, then test both noiseless rank/reconstruction and noisy held-out identification.
candidate_experiment.cost: small-to-medium: four probe-policy arms on existing V24/ReadWrite-style toy worlds, 20-40 seeds

outcomes.if: Adaptive policies win regardless of whether the probe family is structured or unstructured, while fixed structured grids do not
outcomes.then: The bounded-observation survivor should be described primarily as active address selection rather than as a special grid geometry.

outcomes.if: Structured probe families retain an advantage within both adaptive and fixed policy classes
outcomes.then: There is evidence for a measurement-geometry contribution independent of adaptivity, motivating a narrower structural-code claim.

title: When does structural organization predict a downstream functional consequence?
competing_explanations: Fine structural organization changes the effective operator in ways that predict downstream responses beyond coarse connectivity, rank, or spectrum summaries.
Much of the apparent structure-to-computation relation can be captured by simpler coarse summaries; fine developmental placement matters only in sparse special cases.
known: GrowingAnttisNeuron v0 changes developed topographic relation while holding connection count and effective rank fixed.
GrowingAnttisNeuron v1 finds only sparse downstream passive-transfer differences when the cable operator is held identical and input placement changes.
Operaattori compiles detailed morphology into a cable/nonlinear operator that closely reproduces a reference simulator across a morphology panel.
missing_discriminator: A matched perturbation panel where fine structure varies while coarse graph/spectral summaries are preserved, followed by a downstream response or task readout that neither summary can trivially predict.

candidate_experiment.design: Generate or select paired structures with matched node/edge count, effective rank, spectral radius, and coarse path-length statistics but different fine placement/branch geometry. Compile each structure into the same forward operator and test whether fine structure predicts held-out transfer or nonlinear response differences beyond the coarse summaries.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: synthetic paired-structure generator plus existing Operaattori/GrowingAnttisNeuron forward machinery

outcomes.if: Matched coarse summaries still produce systematically different downstream responses that are predictable from fine structural descriptors
outcomes.then: The structure-as-computation motif gains a direct functional bridge between developmental relation and compiled operator behavior.

outcomes.if: Downstream differences vanish once coarse graph/spectral summaries are matched
outcomes.then: The motif should be narrowed: fine structure may encode relation/topography without adding a distinct functional operator beyond coarse summaries in this regime.

title: Does richer state repair/publication control earn its complexity on vector tasks at matched communication cost?
competing_explanations: Separating resident-state repair from publication control provides a robust benefit beyond simple delta synchronization when vector state contains independently reliable and private/relevance-varying components.
Most practical benefit comes from maintaining state and sending sparse innovations; the extra control channels add complexity that disappears once communication budget and task error are matched.
known: ActiveVectorNN preserves most held-out task quality while reducing full-vector communication with the sender state and readout held fixed.
NewMachine shows a clean benefit from factorized repair/publication control when reliability and publication constraints overlap in a scalar-state construction.
missing_discriminator: A common vector-state sender/receiver benchmark comparing delta-only communication against factorized repair/publication control at the same message or bit budget.

candidate_experiment.design: Extend the ActiveVectorNN vector task with independently corrupted components and local-only/private intervals. Compare dense, delta-only, repair-plus-delta, and factorized repair-plus-publication policies along a matched communication-cost frontier using the same recurrent state and readout.
candidate_experiment.cost: small-to-medium: extend existing vector simulation and run 16-32 held-out seeds over a threshold sweep

outcomes.if: Factorized control lowers receiver/task error at matched communication cost across multiple thresholds and seeds
outcomes.then: NewMachine's scalar factorization result generalizes into the persistent vector-state setting.

outcomes.if: Delta-only or repair-plus-delta policies match the factorized frontier once cost is equalized
outcomes.then: The extra publication channel should remain a task-specific mechanism rather than a default persistent-state component.

title: Can a relation learner detect that a previously useful predictive cue has changed meaning before stale authority causes repeated errors?
competing_explanations: Prediction outcomes provide enough online evidence to detect a weakened or reversed cue-to-future contingency quickly, withdraw authority from the stale mapping, and recalibrate while keeping the reusable RGB observable.
Passive outcome monitoring reacts too late in abrupt or sparse-change regimes; reliable adaptation requires explicit uncertainty, change-point machinery, active probing, or an additional observable.
known: Gate 17 shows that no amount of temporal state can predict opposite futures when the observed prefix contains no distinguishing information.
Gate 18 finds a real pre-relapse observable, motion surprise, that reaches 0.90625 held-out balanced accuracy while old confidence-memory states stay near chance.

Gate 19 shows the RGB observable transfers under preserved covariate shift, falls to chance when its contingency disappears, becomes anti-predictive when the contingency reverses, and can recover after small labeled scalar recalibration.
missing_discriminator: A continuous nonstationary world where the surprise-to-relapse contingency changes online and the learner must decide when to distrust and relearn the mapping without being told the change point.

candidate_experiment.design: Run a piecewise world with preserved, weakened, broken and reversed contingencies in a hidden order. Compare a frozen Gate-18 mapping, periodic fixed-window recalibration, passive online change detection, and an active-probe variant. Measure stale-authority errors, detection delay, calibration samples, and recovery of relation decisions after each transition.
candidate_experiment.cost: small-to-medium: reuse Gate-19 generator and add online state/change detection over 20-40 seeded world sequences

outcomes.if: Passive prediction-error/change-point state withdraws authority quickly and relearns the mapping with few stale false-fast decisions across abrupt and gradual transitions
outcomes.then: The measurement-versus-meaning decomposition gains an autonomous adaptation mechanism: keep the observable, monitor its predictive contract, and relearn only the interpretation.

outcomes.if: Passive monitoring either reacts too late or oscillates under weak evidence while active probes or an extra observable materially improve detection at matched cost
outcomes.then: Online causal meaning cannot be treated as a free calibration layer; the architecture needs explicit information acquisition or a stronger uncertainty channel.

notes: This asks when a previously valid interpretation should lose causal authority; it does not assume motion surprise is a universal predictor.

title: Does learned relational structure still save measurements when correspondence confidence must come from image evidence rather than a synthetic tracker?
competing_explanations: The Gate-0→2 savings reflect a reusable mechanism: image-derived correspondence confidence can localize uncertainty and selectively increase sensing while preserving low budget elsewhere.

The savings depend on privileged patch identity and synthetic confidence; once correspondence must be inferred from ambiguous images, the relation prior becomes too brittle or the sensing overhead erases the advantage.
known: Gate 0 shows that a correct relation partition can replace measurements in a world simple on that partition.
Gate 1 learns the relation from ordered common-fate history and matches the oracle future measurement curve after spatial rearrangement.
Gate 2 turns local synthetic confidence into a near-oracle sensing budget while same-cost shuffled confidence fails.

Gate 3 derives confidence from a charged low-resolution image guide: the selected template-margin cue reaches 0.9759 validation balanced accuracy, and adaptive sensing keeps 96.25% success at 55.18%/67.37% of full cost under 4/6 ambiguous guides while matched-cost shuffled confidence collapses.

Gate 4 removes exact relation equality: a cheap current residual projection identifies when local high-resolution content no longer follows the shared relation, and adaptive sensing matches the oracle residual cost curve while equal-cost random extra reads fail.
missing_discriminator: The remaining gap is not synthetic confidence or exact relation equality; it is whether the advantage survives a more realistic sensor/measurement operator, especially when the cheap measurement rows themselves are sparse and may miss sparse innovations.

candidate_experiment.design: Render tracked patches with RGB/texture descriptors, inject occlusion and look-alike alternatives, derive best-match margin and forward/backward consistency from the images, calibrate confidence on training worlds, then test whether low-confidence locations trigger extra measurements that preserve reconstruction quality at lower mean cost than global caution.
candidate_experiment.cost: small-to-medium: synthetic RGB patch renderer plus the existing Gate-2 budget machinery, 40-80 train worlds and 80 held-out worlds per ambiguity level

outcomes.if: Image-derived confidence retains most of Gate 2's success/cost advantage and the shuffled-cue attacker fails at matched measurement count
outcomes.then: The measurement-budget mechanism survives removal of the synthetic confidence oracle and becomes a plausible active-sensing primitive.

outcomes.if: Confidence from image evidence is poorly calibrated or must oversample so broadly that global caution matches its cost-quality frontier
outcomes.then: The current result should remain a synthetic upper bound; useful compression would require a stronger observable or a different sensing policy.

notes: The question is about whether learned structure can safely suppress sensing, not whether a generative prior can hallucinate plausible missing pixels.

Partially resolved on synthetic image evidence: Gate 3 removes the confidence oracle and Gate 4 removes exact relation content, but neither yet establishes the trade-off for sparse physical measurement operators.

title: How sparse can the cheap sensing operator become before compute savings are erased by the extra measurements required to detect relation failure?
competing_explanations: Sparse measurement rows preserve enough random overlap with local innovations that modestly more guide samples retain the adaptive sensing advantage while greatly reducing multiply/add or sensor-mixing cost.

Once each guide measurement touches too few signal coordinates, sparse innovations frequently fall into the measurement nullspace; the required increase in sample count removes the computational advantage.
known: Gate 4 uses eight dense random projections of all 192 high-resolution coordinates per patch and can localize sparse strong innovations almost perfectly.

The uploaded compressed-sensing literature explicitly identifies a price of measurement sparsity: sparse rows reduce storage/computation but can require additional samples for reliable sparse recovery.

Gate 5 runs the proposed row-support × guide-row sweep. Support-1 rows reach only 60% minimum end-to-end validation success and support-2 reaches 92.5% even at 64 guide rows, showing a real price for extreme measurement sparsity.

A moderate support-64, four-row guide uses the same 64 guide scalar samples as the selected dense support-192 guide but 4096 versus 12288 coordinate touches, while retaining 98.75–100% held-out success across the tested innovation levels.

Gate 6 tests the remaining post-hoc-sparsification discriminator. In a one-coordinate innovation regime, coverage-designed support reaches the validation target with 3 rows and 3072 guide coordinate touches, while post-hoc pruning needs 12 rows and 12288 touches to reach the same 100% held-out success frontier.

The dense selected guide uses only 2 scalar rows but 6144 coordinate touches and falls to 93.33% held-out success at the six-innovation level, so scalar sample count and fan-in/mixing work remain distinct currencies.

Gate 7 freezes the Gate-6 sensors and approximately holds innovation energy fixed while increasing innovation support. The three-row coverage-designed sensor still touches 192/192 coordinates but its minimum held-out success collapses from 100% at support 1 to 44.17% at support 2 and 63.33% at support 4.

Twelve overlapping sparse rows remain essentially perfect across the same support sweep, so the missing property is not simple coverage but measurement diversity: multiple signed changed coordinates need independent signatures rather than a single shared row in which they can cancel.

Gate 8 implements the coded-overlap attacker. Degree 2 (six 64-wide sparse rows, 6144 touches) reaches only 87.5% worst validation success, while degree 3 (nine rows, 9216 touches) reaches 98.75% validation minimum and 96.67% held-out minimum across supports 1–64.

At the same 9216 coordinate-touch budget, random sparse 9-row, post-hoc-pruned 9-row and dense 3-row controls all miss the 95% validation target (93.75%, 91.25%, and 93.75% respectively). The older robust 12-row sparse ceiling costs 12288 touches, so regular degree-3 overlap buys the target with 25% fewer interactions.
missing_discriminator: Gate 8 shows that deliberately placed overlap matters at fixed touch cost, but it does not yet distinguish exact coordinate degree from the detailed combinatorics of overlap. Hold degree 3, row width 64 and 9216 touches fixed, then vary coincidence structure between layers.

candidate_experiment.design: Construct four degree-3, nine-row sparse operators with identical row width and total touches: independent partition layers (Gate 8), low-coincidence/expander-like layer pairings, random regular incidence, and an adversarial high-coincidence design that repeatedly groups the same coordinates together. Train matched residual thresholds on the same mixed-support worlds and select no geometry after validation; compare worst-cell validation and held-out reconstruction.
candidate_experiment.cost: small-to-medium: reuse Gate 8 generator and evaluation, four fixed 9-row geometries × 80 validation and 120 held-out worlds per support/patch-count cell

outcomes.if: Low-coincidence or expander-like overlap beats independent/random regular designs while the repeated-grouping attacker degrades
outcomes.then: The next earned mechanism is code combinatorics: not only how many measurements see a coordinate, but which coordinates co-occur across measurements.

outcomes.if: All degree-3 regular geometries are statistically indistinguishable once degree and row width are fixed
outcomes.then: Gate 8's survivor should remain simple coordinate degree/redundancy; extra graph-design machinery is not earned.

notes: This is a cost-quality phase diagram, not a claim that the asymptotic thresholds of any one compressed-sensing paper apply directly to the synthetic image world.
Partially resolved: the designed sparse-measurement price curve is now measured; post-hoc sparsification and natural signals remain open.
Gate 6 advances the question from whether post-hoc sparsification works at all to why the designed sparse operator wins in the ultra-sparse regime.
Gate 7 corrects the Gate-6 coverage interpretation: untouched coordinates are not necessary for failure; signed combinations can disappear by cancellation inside an observed row.

Gate 8 partially resolves the minimum-cost diversity question: degree 3 is sufficient in the tested world and saves 25% of coordinate-touch work versus the robust 12-row ceiling; the remaining question is overlap combinatorics at fixed degree.

title: Can a cheap spatial predictor reduce real diffusion wall time without breaking the globally coherent denoising trajectory?
competing_explanations: The useful mechanism is genuinely local: cheap evidence identifies where the next denoising work matters, and the UNet can be evaluated only on those latent regions plus enough halo to preserve the full-frame update.
The predictor is useful, but SDXL's convolutional/attention computation is too globally coupled or too GPU-inefficient at small crop sizes for spatial sparsity to produce a practical wall-time win.
known: P0 kills independent crop diffusion as the actuator: edge routing is both farther from the full-frame teacher and slower.
P1 shows the selector itself survives: edge-selected 4/16 tiles contain 43.51% of correction energy versus 24.31% for random.
P2 restores global-state semantics and passes: edge masks recover 30.87% versus 17.30% for random, win 9/9 cases, and full-mask parity is exact.

P3 tests actual sparse spatial U-Net execution and fails on validation. Halo 0/4/8 edge recovery is -27.54%/-14.36%/-7.82%, and all three routes are slower than the ordinary full-frame teacher. Halo 8 already has 100% of the full-frame naive spatial-element count, so simply increasing crop context does not restore the P2 semantics.

P4 reproduces DeepCache on the short Turbo route. All tested cache branches are faster (~1.15–1.17× stage speedup), proving that the clock can see reused U-Net work, but the best-quality branch reaches only 72.20% mean recovery with 25.83 dB minimum PSNR and no branch meets the preregistered 80% / 28 dB frontier.

The final component profile shows VAE encode+decode is 445.39 ms / 58.36% of a 763.11 ms stage, while both U-Net calls together are 238.36 ms / 31.24%. This is the systems reason routing the U-Net could not dominate end-to-end speed at this scale.

The final VAE benchmark selects sdxl-vae-fp16-fix on validation and held-out: ~99.5–99.7% recovery with ~1.36–1.38× stage speedup. TAESDXL is ~2.34× faster but far outside the fidelity frontier. The passing 512px speed improvement is therefore conventional VAE engineering, not routing.
missing_discriminator: No further 512×512 Turbo routing discriminator is justified. The tested route is closed: the selector/local-authority result survives scientifically, but no quality-preserving routing speedup was earned. The next compute question moves to independent high-resolution tile workloads where skipping a region deletes an entire diffusion call.

candidate_experiment.design: Move to a new high-resolution question rather than tuning 512px. At 2048×2048, define the all-tile teacher as sixteen independent 512px img2img calls using the fp16-fix VAE, then test whether cheap edge energy can skip 50–75% of those whole calls while preserving the declared quality frontier.
candidate_experiment.cost: one RTX-3060 H0 run over 3 generated photographic prompts × 3 seeds; sixteen teacher tile calls per case

outcomes.if: A <=8/16 edge-selected budget passes validation and held-out recovery/layout/edge/random-margin/speed criteria
outcomes.then: Whole-call omission becomes the first practical WhatToLookAt compute-saving mechanism and must then be repeated on real natural photographs.

outcomes.if: Neither 4/16 nor 8/16 passes
outcomes.then: Stop the high-resolution image branch; the remaining strong domains are streaming/video and physical sensing.

notes: This practical branch is deliberately separate from the synthetic Gate 0–8 measurement experiments.
A speed claim is not attached to P2; it is reserved for P3 or later.
P3 rules out the most literal spatial-compressed-compute implementation: sparse authority does not imply that the U-Net itself can be cut into independent spatial crops.
P4 uses DeepCache as prior art/reproduction, not as a WhatToLookAt novelty claim.

P4 corrects a too-strong P3 timing interpretation: U-Net feature reuse does reduce measured stage time by roughly 0.10–0.11 s, but the savings come with too much output drift to pass the declared frontier.
The profile confirms Claude's qualitative VAE-bottleneck hypothesis, but now with direct component timing rather than inference from warnings or route latency.
The 512px branch is closed after the VAE baseline; no adaptive-cache or additional sparse-UNet gate is earned.

title: Can cheap spatial evidence skip whole high-resolution diffusion tile calls while preserving the all-tile result?
competing_explanations: At high resolution, correction energy is concentrated enough that cheap edge energy can identify tiles worth refining, so skipping 50–75% of independent tile calls preserves most of the all-tile result and directly saves wall time.
Correction energy is too spatially diffuse or too weakly predicted by edge energy; once at least two thirds of tiles must be refined, the selector is not economically useful.
known: At 512px, edge energy consistently localizes future refinement activity, but sparse execution inside a globally coupled U-Net does not convert that information into speed.
The fp16-fix VAE is the earned engineering default for the tile calls, reducing per-call stage cost without changing the routing question.
An independent-tile workload removes the P0/P3 actuator problem: the all-tile teacher itself consists of independent calls, so skipping a tile deletes exactly one operation.

The first H0 implementation is invalidated before scoring: sixteen non-overlapping 512px refinements were pasted edge-to-edge, and the all-tile reference itself showed visible block seams. Agreement with that teacher would not establish coherent high-resolution quality.
missing_discriminator: Use an overlap-blended teacher rather than a hard-paste teacher. H0b uses 25 overlapping 512px calls (128px overlap, 384px stride) whose cosine feather windows form a partition of unity. A selective route starts from the smooth base and adds only selected feathered corrections.

candidate_experiment.design: H0b: 2048×2048 output, 5×5 independent 512px img2img calls with 128px overlap and cosine feathering. Test edge-selected 6/25 and 12/25 claim-eligible budgets plus diagnostic 18/25. Compare with 64 random matched-budget subsets and a teacher-aware greedy recovery reference. Add an explicit teacher-seam validity control; seeds 100/101 select, seed 102 is held out.
candidate_experiment.cost: 25 four-step 512px tile calls per case × 9 cases, plus CPU overlap assembly and exact Gram-matrix subset scoring

outcomes.if: 6/25 or 12/25 passes validation and held-out recovery/layout/edge/random-margin/speed criteria and the teacher seam ratio remains <=2.0
outcomes.then: Proceed to H1 on real natural photographs with the selected overlap-blended budget frozen.

outcomes.if: The overlap-blended teacher itself fails the seam validity control
outcomes.then: Invalidate the tiled-image route again; do not score routing performance against a visibly incoherent reference.

outcomes.if: Only 18/25 is acceptable or no eligible budget passes
outcomes.then: Stop the high-resolution image branch and move to streaming/video or physical sensing.

notes: H0 is intentionally generated-photo evidence only; it cannot establish performance on arbitrary real images.
Timing is measured per independent tile call; selective route time is the sum of the actual selected calls plus selector CPU time.
The hard-paste H0 screenshot was itself the attacker: visual inspection falsified the reference construction before any numeric result was allowed to count.

title: Why does first-ask observer control survive at the local decision but fail across the +256-token continuation?
competing_explanations: The observer is useful mainly at a local commitment boundary: it can select sensor over valve, but keeping the same query intervention active through later tokens perturbs a different copying/follow-through computation and erases the sequence-level win.

The observer is not the main tail problem; copying older source-B details such as K and drifted becomes harder with positional age, so the same locally correct sensor choice still yields a weaker full B continuation even if the intervention is released.

Both effects contribute: positional age changes the downstream basin while tonic observer expression adds a second token-specific disturbance, so phasic release will help but will not fully restore the distance-0 sequence margin.
known: The corrected source-only first-ask anchor is 93 tokens and contains neither the question nor a prior assistant answer; the withheld first-question suffix is 27 tokens.
At distance 0, m=-1 flips the complete sequence to B with A-minus-B summed margin -0.28697 and flips the matched valve/sensor token gap to -0.75; m=+1 favors A, so both first-ask gates pass.

After exactly 256 unreadable masked spacer positions, neutral remains almost unchanged (+11.5491 versus +11.4495 A-minus-B), so the large neutral flip in the earlier visible-filler sweep came from readable intervening conversation rather than masked positional age.

At +256, m=-1 still moves the matched valve/sensor decision farther toward B (token gap -1.75), but the full B sentence loses to A by +0.52131, so local control survives while complete-sequence control fails on this prompt.
missing_discriminator: A matched tonic-versus-phasic tail test at +256: keep the observer on throughout, turn it off immediately after the sensor decision token, and compare both with neutral scoring of the forced-B continuation. This separates observer-induced tail damage from distance/source-copy difficulty.

candidate_experiment.design: Reuse the corrected source-only first-ask +256 masked checkpoint and frozen four-head plan. Score the sensor-B candidate under three matched arms: (1) tonic m=-1 for every candidate token, (2) phasic m=-1 only through the first divergent sensor token and m=0 for the remaining tail, and (3) neutral m=0 throughout while the same B tokens are teacher-forced. Report summed B log-probability, tokenwise tail deltas, source-cache integrity and the A/B sequence margin; do not change the cache, prompt, head plan or candidate text across arms.
candidate_experiment.cost: low-to-medium relative to the completed 8B sweep: one +256 checkpoint and three forced-scoring arms on the already-defined valve/sensor conflict

outcomes.if: Phasic release materially improves the B tail and restores or strongly narrows the full sequence margin relative to tonic, while neutral forced-B is also stronger than tonic
outcomes.then: The current observer should be treated as a boundary-local intervention: persist the intention, recompute the tangent, and pulse its expression rather than steering every downstream token.

outcomes.if: Phasic and tonic tails remain similarly weak while neutral forced-B is also weak at +256
outcomes.then: The dominant failure is ordinary long-distance continuation/copying or downstream basin geometry, not overlong observer expression; EATON remains only a toy gating analogy.

outcomes.if: Phasic helps some tail tokens but not the complete sequence
outcomes.then: The boundary is token/head specific and the next mechanism needs an explicit release policy rather than one global on/off lifetime.

notes: The visible-filler distance run is retained as a re-ask/trajectory confound control, not as evidence for positional decay or amplification.
Neutral is saturated on this prompt, so matched decision-token control and full summed sequence control must remain separate readouts.
EATON v0 does not resolve this question because its tonic failure is analytically built into the synthetic coefficients.

title: How much receiver-conditioned writing survives release-gain and plasticity-calibration controls?
competing_explanations: A modest release gain crosses receiver-dependent calcium thresholds over a physiologically credible range, giving a robust conditional write at fixed spike timing.
The effect is sensitive to the chosen plasticity rates, strong within-burst depression and noisy peak readout; the narrow relative sign reversal disappears under better-calibrated controls.
Receiver-state dependence survives, but a common release-amplitude change explains it fully; no special waveform decoder or transfer of the sender's hidden history is required.
known: OpusPing represents width only as release factors 1 and 1.3 and implements a voltage-gated calcium-threshold write.
H1 passes at 5/6 thresholds; at theta_p=6x, the relative delayed-probe contrast is -10.4% depolarized and -26.2% hyperpolarized.
At theta_p=2x the depolarized broad-minus-narrow probe contrast is +56.6%, while both final weights remain below their initial value.
The L/I ratio is contaminated by plasticity during the burst and small immediate-effect denominators.
missing_discriminator: A calibrated comparison that freezes or disables plasticity, measures the first-spike response before any weight change, and separates final weight from the noisy probe peak while sweeping independently chosen plasticity rates.

candidate_experiment.design: At fixed sender times/count, compare baseline and 1.3x release in each receiver state with plasticity on/off. Record the first-spike EPSP and NMDA calcium trajectory, freeze the final weight for a noiseless standard probe, and repeat a preregistered rate/threshold sweep. Add a control that matches the early EPSP by changing input gain, reporting whether later differences follow the calcium trajectory. An actual sender-waveform-to-release measurement and paired-neuron experiment would be a separate biological step.
candidate_experiment.cost: low for the model controls; a paired-neuron waveform/plasticity experiment is a separate higher-cost follow-up

outcomes.if: A delayed difference remains when plasticity is disabled
outcomes.then: Residual conductance, membrane state or the probe statistic is contributing; the delayed difference cannot all be attributed to a stored synaptic write.

outcomes.if: State-dependent final-weight and noiseless-probe contrasts survive the calibrated rate/threshold sweep
outcomes.then: Keep receiver-conditioned release-to-weight writing as a robust mechanism of this model; biological prevalence and usefulness remain unmeasured.

outcomes.if: The relative sign reversal disappears or a matched calcium/release trajectory explains every difference
outcomes.then: Retain the conditional gain/plasticity result, and narrow any claim of waveform-specific interpretation or receiver-selected net potentiation.

notes: OpusPing cannot distinguish spike width from generic release gain because width has no additional representation in its equations.
A physiological waveform-to-release-to-plasticity demonstration need not encode a complete sender state to be scientifically useful.
This ledger entry records a discriminating follow-up; no new experiment is being added to OpusPing.

title: What predictive information survives when known actions are reversible but the hidden constellation or drift is not observed?
competing_explanations: Learned dynamics-aware low-dimensional predictive states can maintain a calibrated posterior over hidden shapes and infer unobserved changes from appropriately chosen pings, approaching model-informed particle filtering with substantially lower runtime state cost.

Hidden shape and noise are not identifiable under the sparse binary port, so a compact learned state appears successful only because test distributions and ports stay narrow; richer initial probes or a more informative sensor are necessary.
known: MovingTarget2's known-action odometer reverses exact reads without phase access but cannot reverse unknown intervening drift.
Q-word's v3 particle filter sees the same noisy binary observations as learned models and beats the tested qubit-inspired recurrence on three synthetic worlds; it has an advantageous true-law prior.
Two constellations with the same first phase moment can differ under later stronger pings, so present weak-answer agreement alone does not imply predictive-state sufficiency.
missing_discriminator: A matched observation-budget test with initial calibration and delayed strong probes; tune learned recurrent and filtering baselines to validation convergence and equal compute while withholding the true transition law from some filters.

candidate_experiment.design: Train on oscillator configurations with randomized read ports, hidden shape and drift strengths. Give each observer the same number of initial calibration pings and real-time causal bits, then evaluate held-out delayed response families, inverse correction error, uncertainty calibration and CPU latency; compare learned-transition filtering, nonlinear PSRs, exact-action tracker plus learned belief, GRU, qubit-inspired instrument and transformer.
candidate_experiment.cost: CPU-scale simulated oscillator generation; medium retraining/tuning budget and multiple held-out seeds; real physical sensor costs would require separate hardware.

outcomes.if: A compact learned action-odometer-plus-belief model matches calibrated known-law filtering across new ports and unseen drift at matched compute
outcomes.then: Treat the factorization as a useful predictive-memory architecture on this controlled problem, not quantum hardware advantage.

outcomes.if: All observation-only models fail paired hidden-shape delayed probes despite adequate training but succeed with explicit initial calibration
outcomes.then: Record an observability limit: no memory mechanism recovers distinctions not supplied by measurements.

outcomes.if: Quantum-inspired model consistently loses to real-state and learned-filter baselines after equalized tuning and held-out geometries
outcomes.then: Retain exact quantum-instrument demonstrations but reject geometry constraints as an earned general AI memory upgrade.

notes: Current Q-word runs are post hoc exploratory, not preregistered.
MovingTarget2's exact 20-seed result and Q-word's independent 3-seed model-transfer study are distinct experiments.

title: Can active probes recognize an incomplete model instead of confidently choosing a wrong hidden scene?
competing_explanations: Adaptive masks expose useful distinctions even with imperfect transport or an incomplete candidate set, while calibrated absolute predictive fit detects when no available explanation is adequate.
The measured advantage depends on a privileged dictionary and exact transport; adaptive disagreement among wrong candidates can produce confident mistakes.
known: The corrected known-model gate yields 54/64 active, 48/64 random and 7/64 repeat identifications after two additional views.
The selector has the entire candidate dictionary and exact transport, but not the true label.
Varjoluotain's real-photo plate-localization failures show that successful ideal-model simulation does not establish robustness to actual geometry and background light.
Relative posterior confidence over a fixed dictionary does not itself test whether any candidate adequately explains the measured world.
missing_discriminator: Held-out unknown-scene and transport-mismatch trials with a frozen absolute-fit/abstention criterion, equal sensing budgets and disclosed selector computation.

candidate_experiment.design: Omit the true image from some dictionaries, perturb mask position and background transport, and hold out both scenes and mismatch settings. Freeze an absolute predictive-fit threshold on separate calibration data. Compare active, random and repeated views under the same noise and measurement count; include a compute-budgeted active variant. Score identification/log loss for supported scenes, false acceptance and false rejection for omitted scenes, abstention, residual size and cost.
candidate_experiment.cost: Small CPU-scale extension of the NumPy simulator, then a separately calibrated camera/occluder experiment; no large-model training is needed for the synthetic gate.

outcomes.if: Active selection retains a useful sensing advantage and detects omitted scenes at a controlled false-alarm rate on held-out mismatch
outcomes.then: Support a robust active-observer extension and proceed to calibrated physical measurements.

outcomes.if: Active selection becomes confident in incorrect candidates when the true scene is absent or transport is wrong
outcomes.then: Keep the current closed-dictionary result but reject reliable open-world inference until model adequacy and hypothesis expansion are demonstrated.

outcomes.if: The advantage vanishes after matching selector compute or at realistic photon noise
outcomes.then: Retain the observability demonstration while narrowing practical efficiency claims.

notes: The ECG-loop, optical and proposed neural comparisons concern observation choice; they are separate mechanisms and evidence domains.
Dendritic gate learning, retained-state budgets, receiver decoding and read disturbance need separate experiments.

title: Can a downstream reader infer the adaptive question from its available population or rhythm context?
competing_explanations: Self-driven replay, observed neighbouring cells or genuinely shared context can reveal enough of the adaptive threshold to retain its local prediction benefit at a limited communication budget.

Hidden threshold context remains confounded with the signal, so additional spikes mostly supply redundant answers and do not recover the advantage once population size and communication cost are matched.
known: Programmed and learned threshold adaptation reduce prediction error; adaptive branch selection supplies little additional gain in the current learned tests.
Kuulustelu round 4 replays self-driven thresholds exactly under a known rule and common initial belief.
With unseen neighbour-driven context, the sequence-marginalized finite-particle reader has error 0.541 versus the fixed sender's 0.109 using the same estimator family.
Lossless neighbourhood sharing yields 8.2%, below its predeclared 10% benefit; this is a failed magnitude claim, not evidence against all physical fields.
At snapshot c8745f5, round 5 has a population-reader protocol and implementation but no committed outcome receipt.
missing_discriminator: A fresh-world test of population context recovery at matched total bit/compute cost, plus explicit likelihood tests for a rhythmic threshold shift rather than replacing its channel by a Gaussian tag with the same R².

candidate_experiment.design: Keep memory, soma noise, initial receiver information and total communication budget explicit. Compare hidden common-context populations of 1/2/4/8 senders with same-size self-driven and fixed populations and threshold-aware references. Marginalize unknown context, report effective particle counts and confirm on fresh seeds. For a shared rhythm, simulate phase-error distributions and compare direct decoding with the proposed PLV² tag approximation at equal explained variance.
candidate_experiment.cost: Small CPU-scale extension and posterior estimation; larger populations require more bits and decoder work, which must be charged separately from each sender's read count.

outcomes.if: Matched-budget population or shared-rhythm decoding retains a stable advantage on new worlds while posterior estimates converge
outcomes.then: Support a decodable adaptive interface and identify which shared context makes it work.

outcomes.if: Recovery improves only by supplying more redundant bits or the same-R² tag approximation predicts the wrong error
outcomes.then: Keep the self-driven threshold result and narrow claims about population rescue or rhythm acting as an interchangeable label.

outcomes.if: A distant reader remains worse than a fixed sender despite enough observed context and verified inference
outcomes.then: Record a practical communication limit for that adaptive channel rather than declaring local information absent.

notes: Round 5 is Claude's ongoing work; this atlas entry does not modify Kuulustelu or present its preregistered predictions as outcomes.
R²=PLV² for a purely sinusoidal shift under the stated phase-noise assumptions is an explained-variance identity, not proof that its full channel is equivalent to round 4's additive Gaussian tag.
Adaptive coding and decoder context have established prior art, including Fairhall et al., Nature 2001, https://doi.org/10.1038/35090500.
Activity-dependent AIS homeostasis does not by itself establish per-read median thresholding or a universal 50/50 biological firing rule.

title: Can a learned descending renderer close a robust low-resolution visual prediction loop?
competing_explanations: A compact learned world state rendered into the sensor's feature space allows predictions to be corrected across occlusion and changing motion with lower compute than a comparable recurrent video model.
The previous demos are effective because dynamics, phase state and rendering form are engineered; a learned variant may lose to standard optical-flow, Kalman or recurrent baselines.
known: CorticalLoop's fixed 1-D grid loop dead-reckons through a synthetic blackout and fails without signed direction.
Grid discovery via DMD finds linear oscillations from an engineered periodic texture and uses known calibration velocity.
Alavirta corrects an analytic oscillator prediction in Takens delay space and down-weights noisy observations.
Neither repo has an end-to-end learned image renderer or unfamiliar-scene test.
missing_discriminator: Train and freeze a renderer+state filter on low-resolution video, then evaluate on unseen camera scenes and motions, occlusions and corrupted input with matched latency, compute, memory and update budget.

candidate_experiment.design: Use held-out 32–64px camera clips, variable movement and imposed blackouts; freeze training/test split. Compare last-frame copy, optical flow, compact ConvGRU/state-space predictor, and descending-renderer models with/without reliability-gated correction. Score prediction accuracy, blackout drift, relock, uncertainty calibration, fps and GPU memory. Treat choosing where to look as a separate active-sensing ablation.
candidate_experiment.cost: Prototype-scale CPU/GPU; feasibility on a single RTX 3060 is a hypothesis to measure, not an achieved frame rate.

outcomes.if: Renderer-based correction wins under equal budgets on novel scenes and runs continuously
outcomes.then: Support a practical predictive component for a new live AnttisBrain.

outcomes.if: Benefits disappear on unfamiliar motion or the standard baselines match it
outcomes.then: Retain the closed-loop demonstration but reject the new visual architecture advantage.

notes: Present state, next predicted observation and next observation policy must be separately measured.
Functional neuron analogies and analytic phase-tracking results are not evidence of cortical implementation or consciousness.

title: Can a browser recover independently recorded hidden motion through a blocked corner?
competing_explanations: A calibrated edge maps hidden angular motion into a weak spatial camera signal that survives consumer-camera noise and supports direction or trajectory recovery.
The display follows global brightness, exposure, visible motion, calibration leakage or an ideal shared simulation; it does not identify an independently hidden scene.
known: Perjantai has independently reproduced synthetic prediction and precision results, but no measured corner-camera signal.
Varjoluotain uses a calibrated screen/plate/wall operator and its own-forward-model simulations; its real-photo occluder localization fails.
Published ICCV 2017 corner-camera work establishes the physical principle with standard RGB recordings, not this browser implementation.
KulmanTakaa contains only a licence at the reviewed initial commit; its bench and hidden-actor page are planned.
missing_discriminator: Freeze calibration and decoding before independent, genuinely occluded camera recordings; recover hidden direction or different trajectories while rejecting empty-scene, nuisance-brightness and altered-path controls, with no actor metadata entering the decoder.

candidate_experiment.design: First calibrate a luminous phone actor behind a deliberate book/cardboard edge, with a stationary camera viewing only the light surface. Use separately recorded ground truth and shuffled held-out trajectories; keep actor position, animation phase and labels out of the decoder. Compare angular reconstruction with total brightness and generic motion. Include empty hidden scene, visible-side motion, exposure/gain drift, an uninformative ROI and a blocked or altered optical path. Test natural reflected light from a hidden person separately after the emitter bench. Same-model simulations remain implementation checks.
candidate_experiment.cost: Prototype-scale consumer camera, light surface, book/cardboard occluder and a separate phone or screen; camera controls and usable signal strength must be measured.

outcomes.if: Hidden direction or trajectory is recovered on independent recordings and the optical-path/null controls reject the effect
outcomes.then: Support the demonstrated geometry and camera setup; distinguish emitter-bench success from any later ambient hidden-person result.

outcomes.if: Recovery follows nuisance brightness, uses actor metadata, leaks direct views or succeeds only in the shared forward-model simulation
outcomes.then: Reject the real corner-camera claim while retaining any useful implementation or change-detection result.

notes: The development plan is documented in docs/reviews/2026-10-09-perjantai-kulmantakaa.md; it is not an empirical KulmanTakaa outcome.
An edge camera, deliberate pinhole and known plate have different measurement operators.
A fixed prediction residual is not automatically useful for a very weak optical signal; background adaptation can absorb the signal and differentiation can amplify noise.
No universal 0.1% signal amplitude, zero-install novelty or guaranteed phone compatibility is assumed.

title: Does the moon receiver geometry improve memory reading at an equal probe budget?
competing_explanations: Inversion places receiver support at useful locations and makes retained histories easier to distinguish with a limited noisy readout.
Any comparable receiver geometry exposes the same material-dependent wave information; the moon mainly provides an interesting coordinate interface.
known: The wave readout identifies 25/32 held-out variants after 6,000 input-free field steps, tying a 64-feature direct-density reader.
Erasure and disabled coupling reduce the frozen wave readout to 8/32 chance; donor substitution reproduces donor responses.
The inversion map and exact transpose participate in the measured reader, but no equal-budget ordinary-receiver comparison exists.
missing_discriminator: An ordinary-versus-inversion receiver comparison with matched sources, receiver count, time bins, training examples, model selection and noise, evaluated on fresh held-out seeds.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze the material/writing protocol and compare inversion-mapped receivers with ordinary spatial receivers at the same 96-feature and four-source budget. Select receiver and ridge settings using training/validation data only, then precommit fresh test seeds and delays. Include a noise sweep and the same erasure, coupling-off and donor controls; report errors and response separation across several splits.
candidate_experiment.cost: small-to-medium: reuse the dependency-free CPU simulator and add one receiver family, matched fitting and fresh-seed evaluation

outcomes.if: Inversion retains a consistent held-out accuracy or noise-tolerance advantage at equal budgets
outcomes.then: The moon gains evidence as a useful receiver geometry beyond its current role as a working interface.

outcomes.if: Ordinary receivers match or exceed inversion across fresh splits and noise levels
outcomes.then: Retained-state reading remains supported, while inversion should be described as a display/interface choice without a demonstrated retrieval advantage.

notes: This comparison does not settle partial-cue reconstruction, multiple-memory interference or adaptive association; those require separate experiments.

title: Can a blind reader distinguish equal present views through their future consequences?
competing_explanations: Several physically specified probes or delays expose hidden-state distinctions that a single present view cannot reveal, allowing a trained reader to predict held-out consequences.
The apparent distinction is limited to deliberately constructed pairs or queries chosen with hidden-state knowledge; a blind reader gains little at a matched measurement cost.
known: The fixed phi master lens has a 988-dimensional complex nullspace; a designed common rotation distinguishes an initially identical-view pair.
MoonFormer m/-m has identical current density and wave responses, then diverges under g=1.2; g=0 preserves equality across the four measured times.
Neither audit trains a blind query policy or tests unseen state-pair retrieval.
missing_discriminator: A precommitted fresh-state experiment in which the reader sees only measured responses and chooses or receives queries/delays without access to the hidden state, with matched-cost static and temporal controls.

candidate_experiment.design: Generate a panel of state pairs matched on their permitted initial readings. Supply a known forward simulator and independent ground truth outside the reader. Fit readers or query policies on separate training pairs, then freeze and evaluate fresh pairs for state discrimination and prediction of withheld future responses. Compare fixed, random and adaptive queries at the same probe, delay and noise costs; retain symmetry/no-mixing null controls.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: reuse the CPU simulators, add matched-pair generation, observation-only policies and fresh-seed evaluation

outcomes.if: A blind temporal reader predicts withheld responses and distinguishes fresh equal-view states while static and symmetry controls remain ambiguous
outcomes.then: Temporal consequences earn an observable-state identification result beyond the current constructed examples.

outcomes.if: Performance requires access to hidden states, hand-picked separating queries or substantially larger observation budgets
outcomes.then: Keep the current result as an engineered observability example and narrow the adaptive retrieval claim.

notes: This question concerns computational observability; it does not identify a unique source of the physical universe or establish a cognitive experience.

title: Can adaptive state-dependent residue operators outperform matched raw history after fixed residues fail?
competing_explanations: A state-dependent nonlinear cable law gives short residue-like event summaries a useful inductive bias or superior prediction per stored scalar at fixed sensors, training size and compute.

History-based raw features, learned PCA or flexible nonlinear state observers match or beat differences once information and capacity are controlled; residue coordinates add no fundamental information.
known: MondaySihti's full residual transform preserves observation rank exactly, and its three-band compression loses the preregistered hidden-state RMSE comparison in both passive domains.
MondayRepo's fixed causal history and quadratic interactions lower held-out soma-trace prediction RMSE in a known-input seven-compartment model, but do not recover a unique hidden circuit.

MondaySihti G2 was passive; G3 added voltage-dependent nonlinear AMPA/NMDA conductances with hidden stimulation histories and verified future-probe labels. It did not recover unique hidden anatomical sources.

MondaySihti G3 now completed five frozen held-out seeds with nonlinear AMPA/NMDA cable responses and hidden prior input port pairs, verified against the pinned original Operaattori runtime. The three-residue model lost: 0.48023 mV vs raw 0.40357 mV, PCA 0.45765 mV; G3-2 and G3-3 failed.
missing_discriminator: A genuinely operator-adaptive residual learner, compared against capacity- and compute-matched raw-history, recurrent state and learned temporal-feature controls on previously unseen interventions. It must show benefit beyond changing coordinates, track uncertainty in hidden inputs, and report whether any gain survives additional simulator families.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze a small train/validation/test protocol on original Operaattori with new unseen stimulation families. Learn an update rule that changes a measured-residue operator from training data only, then compare future-probe prediction against raw-history quadratic ridge, matched recurrent predictors, ordinary learned filters, shuffled input histories and full-information oracle. Use identical stored state, optimizer steps, data count and selection budget. Retain a full-coordinate invariance control and an exact nonidentifiable case.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: extend existing small simulation and frozen benchmark suite, no biological recordings required

outcomes.if: A compressed residue representation consistently improves fresh held-out prediction at equal information and resource budgets
outcomes.then: Record a useful task-dependent encoding/inductive bias, not creation of information or physical equivalence between image and neuron.

outcomes.if: Matched raw or learned-state controls tie or outperform residual features
outcomes.then: Keep the algebraic bridge and negative compression outcome; do not claim neuron-specific benefit.

notes: Improvement in one constrained simulator would not demonstrate a general brain architecture or real EEG decoding.

The older prespecified nonlinear-but-fixed-residue test was completed in MondaySihti G3 and failed. This question now concerns operator adaptation and stronger baselines, not rerunning G3 with more seeds.

title: Can locally developed geometry improve computation when information must cross branches?
competing_explanations: Development driven by local activity and environment constructs a spatially coupled medium whose nonlinear response to signals at distinct locations improves held-out tasks at equal wiring and readout resources.

A fixed graph, unstructured random tree, or simple uncoupled nonlinear memory computes just as effectively; growth and spatial field coupling add morphology and complexity without measurable task benefit.
known: FieldComputer recovers delayed parity from synthetic nonlinear field activity and from a shared probe, but the uncoupled nonlinear-cell control matches the reciprocal scout-field on both.
VineComputer's 24-generation growth-rule selection usually beats neutral drift on artificial resource collection, but the fixed-start, random-search and direct-optimizer attackers are missing.
GrowingAnttisNeuron demonstrates guided topographic placement relative to shuffled labels while later cable-operator effects are sparse, not a broad morphology-computation advantage.
missing_discriminator: A spatial task provably requiring transfer between at least two locations, where learned growth changes physical interaction geometry; evaluate growth against equal-cost fixed/random/optimized shapes, same-tree passive linearization, no-NMDA, no-transport and no-growth controls on fresh paired environments.

candidate_experiment.design: First publish frozen benchmark worlds, input and output ports, growth budget, trial seeds and behavioral gates. Grow branching cable structures under local rules and compare selection-only, lifetime plasticity, fixed and optimized random/topographic architectures. Compile each morphology into the same independently verified cable or finite-volume forward model, include a state-dependent NMDA or equivalent nonlinearity and separate sites of conditioning and interrogation. Test held-out cross-branch conjunction/location tasks and energy/wiring cost with the same number of measured soma outputs, equal-state readouts, paired worlds and a 16-state local-memory baseline. Evaluate fixed-genome champion, random-search and seven-gene optimizer controls using equal evaluation budgets; report counterexamples and zero-transport limits.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium-to-high: morphology-to-cable compiler plus strict paired generations, frozen new landscapes and simulation controls; can begin on CPU in small graphs

outcomes.if: Growth-generated spatial circuits consistently outperform strong fixed/optimized trees and uncoupled or passive twins on fresh cross-location input tasks at matched wiring, training and readout budgets
outcomes.then: Record a task-specific advantage of developmental geometry as a physical computational resource; do not infer broad biological realism.

outcomes.if: Equal-budget fixed graphs, optimized genomes, local leaky memories or passive twins match the grown structures
outcomes.then: Keep field memory and resource-seeking growth as separate established toy mechanisms; do not call their combination a new neural computer.

notes: This is a proposed future bridge experiment, not an experiment already run in FieldComputer or VineComputer.
Distinct synthetic worlds need paired evaluation for valid first-to-last improvement estimates.

title: Do learned phase transport and error-driven writes protect changing memories beyond signed-real or indexed storage?
competing_explanations: The continuous U(1) edge phase, paths and trained readout afford query-selective update directions that remain useful under longer histories, even when positive and negative signed-real transport, direct vector state, keys and computational work are matched.

Signed-real mixtures, increased writer supervision, a better update acceptance rule or known-key indexing reproduce all observed benefits without complex interference or loop-phase storage; phase-specific advantage disappears outside the two-mark synthetic gate.

Phase advantage depends on short-horizon synthetic image structure; on general histories, quantization/gradient geometry induces drift and stable retention requires stronger addressed storage or retrieval, not more phases.
known: GraphNN's scratch-trained 896-byte phase-only reader recovers 384/384 synthetic A′ and B marks, while the equal-byte gain-only reader recovers 337/384; the missing signed-real *graph* control prevents a phase-specific conclusion.

GraphNN actual A updates have low B sensitivity compared with norm-matched random perturbations, but writing unchanged A already modifies about 85.5% of its bytes; this does not show Wednesday-like compensating gauge writes.
Wednesday's plaquette holonomy and compensated writer are exact constructions with public loop addresses. The 13-byte exact indexed memory stores the random bits perfectly with fewer bytes.

On the 48-byte recurrent test, horizon training through 64 rewrites improves phase mean MSE to 0.1197 versus signed 0.1298, but reader-through-Jacobian higher-order training collapses after one rewrite (MSE 0.851 vs 0.091 for first-order) and does not beat the earlier global writer.
NextLevel's learned remote phase ratio matches direct addressed phase but loses to the 16-byte exact bitset, making retrieval interfaces and budget decisive.
missing_discriminator: A trained 896-byte signed-real transport graph and a trained 896-byte phase-only graph must share the same byte, parameter, write/update and readout budgets; both must face multi-object, many-rewrite histories, incorrect structure, sham writes, genuine query feedback and equal-cost direct addressing. Separately isolate phase-loop flux and finite-write cross-key drift with causal interventions.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze a common many-object sequential rewrite benchmark (1,4,16,64 updates) and a small held-out visual/relational version. Compare phase-only GraphNN transport, a matched signed-real graph with edge values [-1,1], positive gain-only, direct vector, a quantized loss-monotone delta writer, original global writer and exact known-key tables. Match 8-bit state and readout parameter counts and report FLOPs/autograd calls independently. For every write, record target-key improvement, old-key drift, unchanged-input byte changes, and exact per-horizon Jacobian cross terms. In a separate gauge test, apply integer vertex rephasings and loop-flux-preserving versus loop-breaking perturbations at equal byte-change and output-disturbance budgets to test whether loop invariants actually mediate retained information.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium to high: reuse GraphNN and PhaseGraphFastWeightCell trainers, three pilot seeds then 10-20 confirmatory seeds; large 8×8 graph/higher-order runs may require GPU.

outcomes.if: The phase-only graph consistently beats parameter/byte-matched signed-real and strong direct baselines across held-out histories while maintaining low finite-write drift and phase-specific gauge/loop perturbation sensitivity
outcomes.then: Promote a narrow measured phase-transport advantage with the known workload and cost; record phase-specific causal mechanism only if loop controls succeed.

outcomes.if: Signed-real or indexed/delta alternatives match phase at equal update/read cost, or the phase model fails on long histories or novel query structure
outcomes.then: Keep GraphNN's synthetic one-rewrite phase success as a task-specific result, not evidence of a distinct general memory architecture.

notes: The matched signed-real graph is not the same control as positive gain-only edges; phase can express negative edge transport even if no specifically complex interference is needed.
Cross-Jacobian products certify first-order local sensitivity only and do not guarantee finite quantized or 64-step retention.
This question is not a prediction that phase graphs replace Transformers or that closed-loop holonomy is already learned.

title: Can one finite-budget grown planar medium implement changing, content-dependent routing without direct QK computation?
competing_explanations: State-dependent nonlinear local conductances or additional wiring layers permit a reusable spatial circuit to produce useful input-dependent attention at matched cost, as suggested by Limasieni window4 toy recall.

Observed success in unrestricted two-port layouts depends on direct all-pairs wiring, privileged learned bias codes or equal-sized QK-equivalent calculations; restricting to a planar material budget loses the computational advantage.
known: GrowingMatrix's separately optimized planar two-port layout improves over single-port but retains KL 1.93/1.79 on fixed mirror/shift targets after 240 steps.
Limasieni unrestricted two-port layout copies fixed teacher operators nearly exactly; G4 regrows one conductance matrix for each input.
Limasieni G8 broad-initialized nonlinear window4 solves two-seed tiny recall by end-to-end backprop, whereas static attention scores near 0.4 and narrow-init window4 drops to 0.549.
missing_discriminator: One fixed grown spatial network must be evaluated across genuinely unseen content inputs, fixed material and solver budgets, and independent crossing-layer or active-element ablations versus QK softmax and simpler learned input kernels.

candidate_experiment.design: Place eight query ports and eight grounded key sinks on a fixed planar substrate; allow explicitly priced crossover layers or nonlinear local window conductances. Learn one shared circuit on diverse paired key-value retrieval tasks, freeze topology, and score held-out keys/combinations and attention KL plus end-to-end accuracy. Compare static, QK softmax, unrestricted bipartite, a trained planar two-port with no dynamics, and a parameter/compute-matched kernel router; sweep seeds, initialization width, material cost, geometry and query perturbations.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: browser lattice and tiny 8-token numerical tasks, then multiple seeds with measured node/edge growth and compute accounting.

outcomes.if: One shared spatially constrained, cost-matched grown medium dynamically routes unseen content accurately and beats fixed and kernel baselines
outcomes.then: Promote a bounded conditional-operator architecture claim with clearly specified cost and generalization regime.

outcomes.if: Performance requires unrestricted crossings, privileged QK-equivalent bias features, separate per-input regrowth or excessive material/solver cost
outcomes.then: Retain the port-expressivity and narrow input-window demos but reject a competitive reusable grown attention mechanism at this budget.

notes: The source of an input-dependent matrix must be counted as computation; moving QK into an external conductance generator is not removal.
A visually asymmetric current split can arise from a reciprocal underlying network simply by observing different input/output ports.

title: Can small online residue memory restore observed details consistently across future video frames?
competing_explanations: A small updatable memory of actually observed local detail, motion-aligned and addressed by coarse future structure, yields temporal consistency and restoration beyond frame-independent patch regression at the same byte and compute budget.

Apparent gains are already captured by conventional optical-flow-warped previous-frame caching, recurrent CNN baselines, or simply larger spatial priors; Sihti's fixed invertible bands provide no unique memory benefit.

At motion, occlusion, viewpoint or lighting change, the old fine residue is misaddressed or overwritten; temporal reuse creates ghosts and flicker unless uncertainty and occlusion confidence are modeled.
known: SihtiImageModel P3 is translation-tolerant when core+r3 is given; its core-only natural-photo completion is essentially tied with the linear filter and is not online.
SihtiImageModel's photo completion is 25.12 vs 24.87 dB for a linear window filter across 300 held-out photos, not a video result.
Alavirta and CorticalLoop test prediction/correction and direction/blackout only in synthetic oscillator/grid worlds; GraphNN's selective rewrite mark task is not photo or video memory.
missing_discriminator: A held-out short-video restoration study where the memory is written strictly from earlier *observed* frames, with novel occlusion and motion, equal persistent bytes/FLOPs, no target-frame leakage and strong optical-flow cache and learned recurrent baselines.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze low-resolution sequences with repeated moving objects, edits, motion, scene cuts and occlusion; restore deliberately degraded target frames from their permitted coarse target plus preceding seen frames. Compare independent Sihti P3, flow-warped detail cache, patch P3 with online bounded memory, ordinary indexed patch buffer, tiny CNN/GRU and optional graph writer. Match bytes, compute and initial supervision; log per-frame PSNR/SSIM, LPIPS where feasible, temporal warp error, ghosting under occlusion, update speed, bytes and hard new-object adaptation. Add random-frame and shuffled-history controls.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: begin with CPU synthetic sequences and an RTX 3060-scale real-video pilot; 3–10 frozen splits, explicit inference timing.

outcomes.if: Online Sihti residue addressing improves temporal error and reconstruction quality over optical-flow caches and matched recurrent/patch baselines on untouched sequences without severe ghosting
outcomes.then: Record a practical niche for small temporally consistent restoration, with exact dataset, budget and failure boundaries.

outcomes.if: Simple flow-warped cache or recurrent baseline matches/beats it, or useful gains require storing near-full frames or target-derived fine structure
outcomes.then: Retain SihtiImageModel as a bounded spatial completion tool; do not claim a novel temporal memory method.

notes: This is an application hypothesis, not an implemented result. Do not conflate image-internal residue R_k with temporal innovation error between consecutive frames.
When testing own-colour-graph Sihti as a purifier, construct its graph only from the allowed coarse inputs, not from hidden target fine pixels.

title: Do discovered causal groups predict failures beyond simple material or physical sensitivities?
competing_explanations: Causal clustering becomes useful in a nonlinear history-dependent medium where the same edge plays distinct roles by context, improving prospective damage forecasts on genuinely new task families.

Functional groups' performance reflects basic conductance/current structure and labels supplied by chosen interventions; physically informed region or gradient models remain as good, and shuffled controls also succeed.
known: In deterministic Gate 3, balanced groups trained from finite causal edge cuts never have lowest prospective RMSE across six task/arm cases; 110/120 shuffled groupings have lower RMSE.
Gate 1's fingerprint transfers within related terminal shifts but Cross material-only correlation exceeds it.
Gate 2 validation-selected checkpoints limit cherry-picking but uniform material remains competitive on broad held-out terminals.
missing_discriminator: Independent topology seeds and nonlinearly state-dependent routing, plus truly unseen demand families, with causal-group discovery using equal permitted training probes; evaluate prospective held-out finite cuts versus material, flow, sensitivity, spatial and shuffled explanations.

candidate_experiment.design: Build or reuse nonlinear evolving graphs with context-dependent source/sink relations; vary material patterns and independently randomize lattice topology. Fix equal training intervention counts, learn latent edge groups without test family labels, then freeze and evaluate prospective large finite cuts under unseen tasks and context switches. Compare group-based explanations to gradient/Jacobian, material, activity, spatial and randomized group controls at equal access and cost.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium to high: several seeded nonlinear worlds, 10-20 independent topologies plus ablation-sweep costs.

outcomes.if: Learned causal groups consistently outperform equal-access material/current/gradient and shuffled controls on unseen task families and identify damaged components
outcomes.then: Promote a narrow evidence-backed causal-functional grouping result beyond easy linear Kirchhoff structure.

outcomes.if: Simple physical predictors remain as strong or groups fail under unseen contexts
outcomes.then: Keep Growth-Microscope as an excellent falsification/teaching instrument rather than evidence for emergent semantic circuits.

notes: Goodfire's contemporary neural interpretability claims are outside this code's measured domain.
Every group uses three observed training-ablation responses; not unsupervised semantics.

title: Can an inexpensive layout-conditioned detail model recover coherent texture rather than mean blur or independent grain?
competing_explanations: The global layout already carries enough context; a spatially correlated, luminance-aware conditional residue sampler could restore realistic detail without distorting silhouettes, using a small CPU-friendly learned/local prior.

The 8x8 layout discards essential geometry and texture dependencies; without a stronger 16x16 or hierarchical global generative prior, swapping local residual samplers only trades averaged blur for stochastic grain.

The apparent advantage is a mismatch between training/evaluation observers (sharp vs blurry small CNN) or a dataset-format effect, and ordinary upsampling or modern image priors provide the same outcome at lower complexity.
known: On JPEG-mirror CIFAR-10 real 8x8 layouts, P3 beats P0 by +0.107 dB PSNR and misses a +2-point readout criterion.
The frozen learned-layout G1 recognition gate fails (22.7% learned vs 24.1% Gaussian; threshold >=35% and +10 points).

Local conditional mean residues carry only 0.115x real fine-band energy, while sampled code-covariance residues carry 1.59x and reduce judge-feature FD from 110.2 to 97.7 at a ~3.93 dB pixel PSNR cost.
missing_discriminator: A new held-out official-lossless CIFAR-10 test comparing deterministic mean, spatially correlated texture sampling, patch-copy texture, stronger 16x16 layout, and matched ordinary upsampling, with class/layout scoring calibrated to resolution, realistic texture metrics, fixed byte/compute budgets, and cross-seed consistency.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze original and lossless training/testing splits before model selection. Match layout capacity, patch-memory parameter count and runtime where feasible. Evaluate real-layout and generated-layout tasks separately: pixel PSNR/SSIM; high-frequency energy and spatial correlation; feature distance calibrated across sharp/blurred domains; blinded sample quality; class conditionality versus Gaussian baselines. Include a zero-texture and independent-colour-noise control to detect reward hacking; keep predeclared stop gates.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium (one RTX 3060-class machine; begin with small CPU-fixed sampler controls)

outcomes.if: A coherent local sampler improves texture correlations and held-out distributional distance at matched cost without large structural or class-control regressions
outcomes.then: Record a bounded benefit for conditional texture given layout, not a general generator breakthrough.

outcomes.if: Simple patch copy or a stronger coarse layout matches/exceeds it, or realistic texture requires much heavier learned modeling
outcomes.then: Close SihtiImageModel2 as an informative decomposition and negative-control experiment; do not add complexity for its own sake.

notes: Distinguish source-supported G1 failure from later post-hoc interpretations; official CIFAR files were not used for recorded scores.
