No promise to build the proposed experiment; this is an unresolved question archived with the source.

title: Can a learned dendritic operator preserve useful new histories at competitive memory cost?
competing_explanations: History-dependent conductance enables selective, interference-resistant readout from few somatic probes, even across new history families.
The four familiar contexts merely allocate an overparameterized slow tag to an easy supervised readout; a two-bit table or compact recurrent baseline suffices.
known: A 512-episode held-out four-context somatic readout passes 100%; frozen and erased controls approach chance.
The current system has 21 floating slow states (168 bytes) to distinguish just four contexts, and uses one fixed designed probe.
missing_discriminator: Freeze writer/reader rules and test unseen histories, orders, delays and probe families with equal-information baselines, exact table/codebook and matched-state recurrent learners; count full state and computation.

candidate_experiment.design: Register novel combinations and delayed competing writes, randomized morphology, variable probes, and forget-and-relearn challenges. Compare learned shunt with fixed-state RNN, direct-address table and immutable tree under equal bytes and energy; compute interference, latency and accuracy across independent seeds.
candidate_experiment.cost: low to medium CPU experiment

outcomes.if: New histories transfer while avoiding interference and beating byte-matched direct and recurrent controls
outcomes.then: Promote a bounded advantage for history-shaped one-port response memory.

outcomes.if: Only preassigned four labels remain separable or cheap explicit storage dominates
outcomes.then: Retain SolsBaby as a useful causal visualization, not efficient general memory.

notes: All present values are engineered and dimensionless; no biological validity follows from this gate.

title: Will genuine offline successor-map replay rescue long-range decisions without cosmetic theta gates?
competing_explanations: A bounded replay process propagates sparse experience to distant states and improves need-dependent decisions under fixed exploration budgets.
More experience, altered discounting or direct graph planning explain the benefit; adding a theta flag is unnecessary.
known: G1 latent learning and G4 shortcut pass under preregistered controls.
G2 misses its need-switch threshold, G3 septal ablation fails its kill rule; seven of ten G4b trials have matching step-cap failures.
Post-hoc doubling exploration with a longer horizon improves far correctness to 76.5%, while increasing discount horizon alone does not.
missing_discriminator: Preregister offline replay separate from additional exploration; compare equal-transition replay, matched extra walks, direct shortest-path planning and no-replay under held-out distance changes with visible map propagation.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze the same experience history, hold map/agent capacity constant, then allocate controlled offline transition backups versus no rest, matched new experience, and planning baselines. Test distant goals and newly opened doors over many worlds while requiring an actual septum ablation effect if claimed.
candidate_experiment.cost: low; browser/Node experiments across seeded maps

outcomes.if: Replay consistently improves distant need choice under fixed external experience and matched computation
outcomes.then: Add replay as a causally supported module with an explicit operating regime.

outcomes.if: Only more walks or direct planning work, or theta remains immaterial
outcomes.then: Retain the failure gates and avoid assigning a computational role by biological name alone.

notes: Replay is a proposed next component, not a demonstrated part of ClaudesBaby.

title: Does interference destroy LiveMode's stored colour or make its frozen Qwen reader misread it?
competing_explanations: The matrix still retains the target colour, but a lift trained on clean short episodes is misaligned with the noisy memory vectors encountered after interference.
Interfering writes destroy the target distinction in the matrix itself; changing only the reader cannot restore information that is no longer there.
known: Gate 2 records 100% strict accuracy on 400 latest-rewrite evaluations using supplied addresses, colour codes and a trained lift.
Gate 3 removes the latest-write shortcut: at 32 slots/500 writes, strict accuracy falls to 37.5% while oracle-code injection stays at 100%.
The existing Gate 4 design and source compare an equally trained clean reader and interference-trained reader and report direct-matrix colour accuracy, but no real-Qwen Gate 4 result is committed.
missing_discriminator: Paired direct-memory recall and Qwen-answer measurements on fresh interference episodes, with equal offline training budgets for the clean and robust readers.

candidate_experiment.design: Run the existing Gate 4 controlled comparison with Qwen and the 1,024-byte writer fixed: original lift, equal-budget extra clean training and interference training. On untouched names/seeds report direct-memory four-colour accuracy alongside strict Qwen answers, erased/stale/wrong-address controls, oracle code and dictionary context.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: existing implementation; one local GPU calibration/evaluation run, with supervised adapter training counted separately

outcomes.if: The direct matrix retains the colour and the robust reader improves over the equal-budget clean reader
outcomes.then: Reader alignment explains part of the loss; the result remains a supplied-address four-colour interface, not autonomous memory.

outcomes.if: Direct-matrix accuracy collapses with load and a robust reader cannot recover the target
outcomes.then: The bottleneck is at least partly destructive storage interference; a reader-only remedy is insufficient.

notes: The Gate 4 design follows Gate 3 and is labelled a hypothesis, not independent preregistration.
No byte or compute advantage over exact dictionary retrieval is presumed.

title: Can an early subject-specific intervention carry a remembered property beyond a generic same-size push?
competing_explanations: A name's representation gives a property intervention privileged access to downstream subject-related computation, but the useful direction/layer/gain is restricted.
Earlier-token interventions mainly leak a large colour bias forward; apparent subject advantages depend on gain, direction and the small reused prompt set.
known: Naula N2 remains OPEN: J-lens/gain 8 gives 56.7% name-site versus 48.4% unrelated-word four-choice accuracy.
WhereToWrite's logit-lens/gain-2 result gives 42.25% name-site versus 45.25% unrelated-word accuracy across 400 evaluations but only 95 distinct cases.
N5 verifies name-token decodability for a particular reader; it does not establish subject-specific causal routing.
Answer-site steering is easy and must be separated from native associative retrieval and downstream reasoning.
missing_discriminator: A frozen protocol on unseen names and prompt families, with same-direction/same-norm position controls and causal attention-head interventions that selectively remove any subject advantage.

candidate_experiment.design: Choose direction, layer, gain and candidate transport heads on development data only, keeping J- and logit-lens experiments separate. Freeze them, then evaluate each new name/prompt/colour case once with subject, unrelated-token, answer, random and wrong-colour arms; record every prediction and ablate the nominated heads.
candidate_experiment.cost: medium: frozen 0.5B Qwen GPU inference plus development-only head attribution; no backbone training

outcomes.if: A subject advantage transfers to unseen cases and is selectively removed by the nominated head ablation
outcomes.then: The specific routing hypothesis gains causal support, bounded to the tested sites, direction and model.

outcomes.if: The advantage disappears on unseen prompts or unrelated-position pulses match it
outcomes.then: Retain generic perturbation as the simpler account; name decodability alone did not provide a usable memory route.

notes: Do not pool Naula J-lens/gain-8 and WhereToWrite logit-lens/gain-2 results as matched replications.
The historical 400-evaluation independence-based confidence interval is invalid and does not enter this question's evidence.

title: Can a changed response operator protect selectively rewritten memories beyond normalized fast weights and explicit addressing?
competing_explanations: A nonlinear coupled response operator can use global graph structure to reduce interference between nearby bindings beyond a degree-normalized matrix reader at matched storage and compute.
The observed gains are mostly elementary normalization; exact indexed addressing and conventional fast-weight correction remain better for arbitrary keys.
known: V2 stores a small response difference in conductance after voltage reset, but does not test scalable associative rewriting.
AIBrain's 2,048-byte graph loses at load 32 (71.9%) to equal-size Hebbian fast weights (95.4%) and shows 42.5% untouched retention after rewrites.
AIbrainV2's preregistered 512-byte comparison beats raw fast weights by 10.17 percentage points, but a post-result degree-normalized read captures most of that gain.
At AIbrainV2's tested 8–64 random bindings, an indexed lookup stores just 3 bytes each and beats the graph.
missing_discriminator: A genuinely independent, preregistered longer-horizon selective-rewrite test with identical storage and read/write compute, normalized matrix and properly budgeted index/hash baselines, and unseen association sequences.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze writer/read hyperparameters on development seeds; run A→B→A′ and multi-interference sequences under fixed byte, query and energy budgets. Compare graph Schur reader, degree-normalized/optimized fast weights and packed indexed maps; separately track changed-binding quality, untouched retention, normalization and exact lookup cost.
candidate_experiment.cost: low: NumPy CPU matched-seed associative-memory task, with careful storage/time accounting

outcomes.if: Operator response consistently preserves untouched associations while matching new-binding accuracy beyond the best normalized and indexed controls at equal budget
outcomes.then: Keep operator-memory selective rewriting as a distinct engineering mechanism within the demonstrated regime.

outcomes.if: Normalized direct reads or indexed stores match or beat the graph after fair tuning
outcomes.then: Attribute the observed gain to standard normalization/addressing rather than a special response-geometry memory.

notes: Do not reuse AIbrainV2's post-hoc normalization comparison as if it were preregistered.
No lossless image encoding or biologically faithful dendrites are assumed.

title: Can a phase-aware reader turn complementary branch probes into better causal object tracking than a velocity model?
competing_explanations: Complementary state-conditioned phase measurements carry directional information that a phase-aware multi-column receiver can exploit for motion prediction.
The demonstrated two-phase gains are only an observability trick for a fixed small classification task; a simple velocity predictor already uses available history better.
known: Gate 1 adaptive and preset complementary probes both classify three soma-matched patterns at 100% in a controlled toy.
Gate 2's phase-blind two-ping average algebraically cancels direction (difference ≈3.3e-16).
In 32 noisy moving-bar movies, adaptive/preset/symmetric next-frame recall is 0.615, while a simple two-frame velocity forecast achieves 0.781.
missing_discriminator: Preserve the two separate phase channels causally at the receiving column, then compare prediction errors and compute/pulse budgets to the velocity baseline and direct sensory histories on new trajectories.

candidate_experiment.design: Hold movie generation, train/test seeds and two-ping budget fixed. Give the receiver signed phase channels rather than their mean, and compare a learned linear temporal receiver against a same-size velocity/history model plus shuffled-phase and symmetric controls.
candidate_experiment.cost: low: existing 16-column CPU movie model with a phase-aware receiver

outcomes.if: Phase-aware receiving beats the two-frame velocity control on new trajectory seeds without extra information or computation
outcomes.then: Promote temporal probing from hidden-state visibility to supported causal tracking utility.

outcomes.if: Direction survives mathematically but prediction does not improve over velocity/history models
outcomes.then: Keep the first gate as an observability result and the tracking advantage unsupported.

notes: V3's Gate 2 is an explicit failed tracker test; no tracking advantage is inferred from Gate 1.

title: Can the medium choose useful memory writes and beat a conventional continual learner?
competing_explanations: A local traffic/eligibility signal can choose a writable site and retain useful content with less interference under an external task.
Engineered gates implement ordinary addressed storage; a conventional learner or indexed store matches the behavior more cheaply once allocation and read costs are counted.
known: Both Alexander implementations still supply the address and desired value.
Sol analog address trace ties a discrete latch; ordinary wells are perfect on the bounded array task.
BrainBoxSol persistent slowness retains old traces but fails replacement adequacy.
missing_discriminator: A preregistered external continual-associative-recall task with no experimenter-supplied internal addresses or desired internal states, matching persistent bytes and read/write compute to a conventional learner; report fresh binding acquisition, untouched retention, overwrite accuracy and time.

candidate_experiment.design: Choose benchmark and conventional baselines before model changes. Supply identical external observation/reward streams, permit every learner to select its own storage, and compare on unseen interference/reversal sequences under fixed bytes and query/compute budgets. Freeze on development seeds before fresh outcomes; include frozen/shuffled traffic and explicit-address upper bounds.
candidate_experiment.cost: A bounded CPU benchmark is feasible; this is a proposal only, with no implementation or performance result.

outcomes.then: Retain the bounded learned-allocation mechanism and document which control it beats.
outcomes.if: A traffic-driven writer wins acquisition and untouched retention at matched cost on fresh sequences

outcomes.then: Close the advantage claim and retain only the working memory component.
outcomes.if: An ordinary learner or indexed baseline matches or beats it

notes: The proposal is unbuilt. Re-deriving a memory bank does not establish near-optimality.
Energy advantage requires an explicit energy model or measurement; operation counts alone are insufficient.
Task supervision is allowed; hidden experimenter-selected memory addresses or states are not.

title: Can incomplete visible Sihti context locate genuinely missing image detail better than global or same-band lookup?
competing_explanations: Cross-scale visible neighborhoods supply discriminative addresses for selecting useful local residue donors even when global image similarity is misleading.
Any small reconstruction improvement comes mostly from donor-pool coverage, smoothness or generic regularization; same-band or whole-image retrieval suffices and learned binding adds little.
known: DoDis v1 learned binding gives 0.01417 MSE on 12 birds, but shuffled binding reaches 0.01438 versus memory+smoothness 0.01494.
DoDis v2 changes from whole-image donors to independently addressed local donors, with same-band-only and masked-mean comparators.
One hundred per-bird v2 receipts and a large aggregate JSON were found in the public run folder, but the aggregate performance has not been verified in this atlas.
SihtiGraphModel's v3 classifier surrogate fits individual image/mask distributions well at p=.90 yet does not transfer its learned tile locations between its two selected birds.
missing_discriminator: Audit DoDis's already-committed v2 results against its preregistered 100-bird protocol and report paired confidence intervals, leakage checks and outcome by image. If incomplete, rerun exactly the locked design before introducing new hyperparameters.

candidate_experiment.design: On the same 100 held-out test-bird masks and donor bank, compare masked mean, whole-image donors, same-band-only local addresses, cross-scale local addresses, local+learned binding, local+shuffled binding and local+CNN purpose; inspect stored per-image MSE, true CNN margin, provenance and runtime, with paired confidence intervals. Preserve v1 as a separate 12-bird result.
candidate_experiment.cost: Low to moderate: first parse and validate the published 100-bird results.json; new GPU work only if stored receipts are incomplete or invalid.

outcomes.if: Cross-scale local retrieval beats global, same-band-only and masked-mean on new withheld pieces with meaningful paired uncertainty; binding further beats shuffled graph
outcomes.then: Keep the bounded visible-context content-address mechanism and report separate evidence for relation learning.

outcomes.if: Global/same-band/no-repair matches local retrieval, or shuffled graph matches learned graph
outcomes.then: Retain donor-coverage/regularization controls and close the corresponding stronger learning advantage claim.

notes: Ground truth hidden residues may score reconstructions but must not be used to choose donors.
Classifier margin is a separate metric and can worsen actual pixels.
Do not infer v2 success from the existence of 100 JSON files.

title: Can a frozen webcam lens recover new hidden-side positions from optical evidence rather than priors, continuity or auto-exposure?
competing_explanations: Hidden motion modulates observed wall reflections or cast shadows through a stable, spatially discriminating optical path, so a learned lens can infer some never-trained hidden positions.
The plausible hidden-half image is explained by continuity over the split line, auto-exposure, correlated room brightness, temporal scene priors or extrapolation of familiar training configurations.
known: The saved synthetic glow and shadow test improves 1/8-resolution change R² from 0.550 to 0.728 when an edge carries extra spatial structure, against −0.074 for independent halves.
The synthetic continuation and exposure controls give full-resolution R² 0.963 and 0.985 respectively, without demonstrating non-line-of-sight geometry.
A novel-colour synthetic probe fails full-resolution R² at −10.516, and the documented novelty detector threshold was changed after seeing that control.
A user-observed webcam image showing an unfamiliar position is not by itself a frozen, controlled real-world optical-reconstruction score.
missing_discriminator: Record genuinely new hidden-only positions and objects in a room with fixed and measured exposure; score a lens trained on disjoint movement/lighting episodes, using causal occluder insertion/removal and temporally shuffled, global-brightness, continuity and scene-prior baselines.

candidate_experiment.design: Choose one visible-wall/occluder setting, predeclare novel hidden-only motion trajectories and train/test sessions. Freeze before test, ensure no arm/object crosses the half-image split, log camera exposure and global brightness, then alternate an occluder while retaining the same hidden actions. Compare matched-compute linear and CNN predictors against brightness-only, random-time-pairing, continuity and static hidden-scene baselines. Report true hidden-pixel and coarse-shape R² with uncertainty and replay videos.
candidate_experiment.cost: Low-to-moderate: OddOne webcam, a door edge or chair occluder, printed coloured targets and a fixed protocol, no model-scale GPU training required.

outcomes.if: Unseen hidden-only positions outperform all optical-irrelevant controls on fresh sessions, and the spatial advantage vanishes on removing the occluder
outcomes.then: Retain a bounded real-room indirect optical-sensing mechanism, specifying only measured channels and resolutions.

outcomes.if: Global exposure, continuity, stationary priors or randomized temporal pairings explain the recovery equally well, or novel positions collapse
outcomes.then: Keep OddOne as a useful predictor/demo but close the claim that it reads a physically hidden scene in that setup.

notes: Real webcam observations require temporally separated held-out episodes; frame-prequential labels do not imply independent samples.
The synthetic novelty cutoff was tuned after feedback, so freeze diagnostics before a real-data gate.

title: Can a resonant cavity acquire persistent wall memory from experience and later read it with fewer calibrated probes than ordinary indexed storage?
competing_explanations: Local experience-dependent wall updates can construct stable reusable information, while a finite-speed scattering geometry bounds the response combinations a listener must calibrate and a cheap known probe retrieves them.

All demonstrated capability comes from externally written spring settings plus a deliberately engineered decoder; a conventional indexed memory and fixed readout reproduces or exceeds the useful function once writing, retention and readout costs are counted.
known: ResonantNeuron's early arithmetic used designed interference weights and gates, rather than learned persistent material changes.
Kavitaatio's wall spring settings persist after waves die but are externally assigned; multiwall echoes are not additive.

WallMemoryLaw's pre-registered K24 stadium reports 300/300 held-out 24-bit words from an amplitude-pruned 848-state calibration in a constrained numerical window, with additive and degree-2 controls failing.
ResonanceAsControlledMethod's new-geometry parabolic beam loses to source-tuned fixed-angle controls, and BigKahuna's adaptive needle loses to a fixed probe while both show that asking can help.
missing_discriminator: A matched write–retain–read demonstration in which local observations and an explicitly defined feedback signal cause the cavity boundary to change and persist without an experimenter writing the target bit pattern, followed by novel mixture recognition at matched material-state capacity, calibrated probes, hardware/compute cost, noise and delay versus ordinary indexed memory.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze task/environment, write rule, geometry, probe selection and baseline before evaluation. Introduce an explicit learnable local spring adaptation process, with limited wall energy and bounded parameter magnitude. Train from temporal streams with unknown record identities; remove drive, let wave field decay, and query under novel mixtures. Compare fixed and active probes, unmodified springs, pre-addressed write upper bound, identical-capacity indexed store and equal-parameter standard online model. Score separate acquisition/overwrite/retention/interference, wall wear, calibration-state count, read/query cost and held-out error.
candidate_experiment.cost: Moderate numerical simulation first; hardware adaptation and energy claims require a separate physical implementation.

outcomes.if: The local writer retains separable records and reads them at equal or lower full costs on fresh tasks than conventional controls
outcomes.then: Preserve a bounded write–retain–read mechanism and publish which part of the advantage comes from the physical medium.

outcomes.if: The locally updated wall forgets, cannot address records, or a matched fixed/indexed baseline wins
outcomes.then: Keep the successful forward scattering calibration law and close the stronger physical-learning/readout-advantage claim.

notes: Published OpenAI Euclidean-wave local smoothing does not prove a cavity memory writing or discrimination theorem.
Reuse WallMemoryLaw's causal-tour calibration as an available model, not as permission to supply hidden target wall bits.
Evidence above is source-reported repository results, not independently rerun by Genealogy.

title: Does the paper-inspired focus center anticipate nonlinear field reorganization better than ordinary gradient or kinetic activity?
competing_explanations: An interference-sensitive free-wave lift identifies asymmetric wave concentrations that precede later movement, splitting, or disappearance of a positive-field region beyond ordinary field-activity measures.

The magenta focus centroid and green CoM are different spatial weights on the same deforming field; apparent crossing or anticipation comes from shifts in mass, wraparound, multimodal circular-center instability or ordinary kinetic/gradient wave activity, with no incremental diagnostic benefit.
known: AnttisInstanton2's 256 independent equal-power free-wave reference found no reliable improvement in future global L4 prediction from adding its fixed-fiber auxiliary response to ordinary L4, energy flux and phase controls.
The newer nonlinear live viewer measures spatially separated periodic center trajectories and gradient/kinetic controls but does not yet report a held-out predictive score or stable lag effect.
Slider3's 64 phase trials prove phase sensitivity versus power alone but an ordinary three-delay sensor and complex coherent intensity detect those same changes.
The conserved-current theorem applies to free waves, not to the evolving nonlinear phi-four substrate or its derived centroid.
missing_discriminator: A frozen, independently seeded nonlinear multi-run protocol predicting future center motion or local domain-wall reorganization from equal-history observers, with confidence-filtered circular centroids and ordinary gradient/kinetic/phase-aware baselines; all forecasts evaluated before outcomes on held-out runs.

candidate_experiment.design: Freeze 20–50 independent initial conditions and a lag horizon before inspecting tests. Sample both phi and velocity, compute four centers plus local energy and phase measures, and record full field snapshots. Discard undefined centers by a declared mass/coherence gate; use periodic displacement in all methods. Train an identical time-history predictor on early seeds for green next-step velocity, region split/merge and boundary-motion targets. Evaluate paper focus vs gradient/kinetic and ordinary phase-coherent energy under matched compute and identical input history. Include lag and time-shuffle controls, a peak-tracker alternative and within-event bootstrap by independent seed.
candidate_experiment.cost: Moderate local CPU/GPU numerical simulation and analysis; no physical setup required.

outcomes.if: The focus adds statistically clear held-out skill beyond phase-aware ordinary controls across independent seeds and retained validity strata
outcomes.then: Retain a narrowly predictive nonlinear observer (not a new particle or extension of the free-wave theorem), with effect size and compute cost.

outcomes.if: The focus supplies no incremental skill or its lead disappears under confidence gating, matched periodic tracking or shuffled timing
outcomes.then: Keep a useful interference visualizer and close the stronger anticipation claim.

notes: No causal interaction between the two markers is encoded in the field evolution.
Overshoot should mean signed separation relative to the instantaneous green velocity, not merely passing on an X plot.
This Genealogy entry is based on repository source and saved results, not independent benchmark reruns.

title: Can a locally written, blindly ping-read medium sustain two robust inherited states rather than select a single dominant one?
competing_explanations: A receiver that averages analog evidence before thresholding, or two distinguishable positive material signals, creates two stable basins under contamination; fresh scouts can reproduce both writing policies using the medium alone.

The reported readout mainly sees material-value histograms; spatially correlated local pings and writer mixing erase one schedule's signature, so generations inevitably collapse or require hidden engineered labels and stronger-than-comparable storage capacity.
known: Evening's equal-total order experiment scores 1.000 with 16 or 8 blind pings on 48 fresh worlds but the successful reader still scores 1.000 when spatial structure is shuffled.
Recency ping accuracy is 0.625 (p=0.18) on 32 worlds while the simple mean-material scalar scores 0.812, retracting the earlier claim of scalar-blind recency.
Under the tested reader, pure avoid-first survives 0/8 lineages, or 2/8 with designed quorum, versus 8/8 seek-first; generation map f(0.05)=0.379 shows asymmetric contamination.
The repo analytically proposes a stable low-p fixed point after 9 independent averaged pings/site, but that experiment has not been run and wall correlation weakens the independence assumption.
missing_discriminator: Run a frozen independent-seed comparison of 1, 4 and 9 analog pings averaged per site before thresholding versus the existing vote, with spatially separated probes and measured correlation; separately add a balanced two-presence writer and matched direct-statistic, non-wave and indexed-memory baselines. Require both initial states to reproduce for multiple generations under contamination without direct copying.

candidate_experiment.design: Pre-register an 8+8 lineage protocol for all-avoid and all-seek ancestors over at least eight generations, with held-out writer seeds, fixed ping budgets, identical readout capacity and balanced training examples. Measure the empirical f(p) near p=0 and p=1, state-transition error and stability under deliberate 1–5% contamination. For a two-material design compare matched scalar probes, direct access to local material, no-wave controls and ordinary indexed copying. Release per-generation responses, confusion matrices and resource/budget accounting.
candidate_experiment.cost: Modest numerical simulation; an actual physical medium would require separate hardware tests.

outcomes.if: Both pure schedules maintain reproducible stable basins under held-out contamination and outperform matched simple-material readers at comparable cost
outcomes.then: Retain a bounded medium-mediated inheritance mechanism with separately identified value of the wave reader.

outcomes.if: One state still collapses or matched direct statistics reproduce all benefits
outcomes.then: Keep the useful blind reading instrument but close the stronger binary heredity and wave-specific advantage claims.

notes: No direct gene copy in Evening's current loop, but reader training and schedule vocabulary are externally specified.
WallMemoryLaw's discrete reflecting-wall calibration is not the same PDE or a guaranteed result for Evening's distributed Klein–Gordon mass.
Results are source-reported; Genealogy has not rerun them.
